payload.friendly_name: Nightly SonarCloud and per-PR complexity gate
payload.purpose_context: The 2026-11-03 test suite assessment found that nothing in the charter's build measures complexity, duplication or security patterns. The operator ruled that Checkstyle complexity rules gate each pull request and that SonarCloud runs nightly and reported only, with new-code coverage, never as a required check. This mission implements that ruling without adding a Gradle plugin, and lands before the SonarCloud project exists.
payload.purpose_tldr: Add a complexity gate to every pull request and a nightly, reported-only SonarCloud scan, as Proposed ADR-0056 records.

options: Ceiling just above today's worst (near-zero entries)
Strict norms (CC 10, NPath 200, 50 lines) + large register
payload.question: Which Checkstyle complexity limits should gate each pull request?

payload.final_answer: Core-aligned limits + shrink-only register: CyclomaticComplexity 15, NPathComplexity 1000, MethodLength 60, NestedIfDepth 1, on main and test; existing violators as shrink-only suppressions with a reason each

payload.question: Do FR-001..FR-005 (Checkstyle complexity gate; nightly sonar.yml with generic scan action; skip green without SONAR_TOKEN; reported only, never required; docs) match the intended scope, with #239, per-PR Sonar and project/token creation out of scope?

options: Method-scoped XPath entries + a Gradle stale-entry check in verifyAll
Format/Size/sunset guard only; staleness caught at sunset
payload.question: How is the complexity exception register kept shrink-only (stale entries detected, new methods not exempted)?

payload.final_answer: XPath per method + stale check: suppress-xpath entries in the one suppressions.xml naming each method; a build-logic Gradle check re-runs Checkstyle (the build's own plugin) over the register's files with the filter off and fails verifyAll on a stale entry or a wrong Size; engineering alignment confirmed
